publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.0 changes how you add and edit monitors and hands confirmed incidents to Oncall. New monitor starts from your website and offers other ways to add: fill in the form, paste URLs or a CSV, import a file, follow a service's status, or discover from DNS, a spec or deploys. One form serves new and edited monitors, with Up or down rules added one at a time and rarely changed settings under Advanced. Locations lists where checks run from, and Add location gives one command for any machine with Node 22.13 or later. Settings › Alerts holds destinations, who is told by default, root-cause categories and Sent alerts. A webhook destination in the Oncall handoff format sends confirmed failures, reminders and recoveries to Oncall; Sent alerts shows Acknowledged, Received and Responded separately, and Received and Responded stay Unknown because Oncall offers no way to read them yet. Signed-webhook alerts retry with the same delivery ID, a route can name up to three fallback contacts, and contacts can have quiet hours. Saved Site24x7 and Better Stack monitors convert, Pingdom tags become labels, and saved UptimeRobot outage history imports through the API and command line as separate source history, not yet shown in the console. Settings › People adds members with roles, second factors and keys. Sensitive actions, such as downloading a backup or adding a destination or location, now need a second factor verified in the last five minutes, and the console does not yet ask for it at sign-in. Scheduled reports, page-speed monitors, a consented real-user beacon, a third-party status catalog and discovery from DNS, specs and deploys are also new. 26 additive migrations (0057 to 0083), no new required settings, and @runeditrun/rer is pinned to exactly 0.2.94. Back up before upgrading; monitors, history, incidents, destinations and private settings are kept. Known issue: a response body over 64 KiB still fails the check, so monitor a smaller page such as a health endpoint. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before this release's console changes.
